problem: Prior VLN methods lack explicit supervision for matching sub-trajectories to their corresponding sub-instructions, so fine-grained cross-modal alignment is learned only implicitly through the navigation loss.
motivation: At each step the agent must attend to a particular sub-part of the full instruction to choose its next move. Without explicit alignment supervision, attention and representations may drift from the relevant sub-instruction, which hurts decision-making.
key_idea: Add two auxiliary constraints, an Attention Alignment Constraint and a Representation Alignment Constraint, that supervise sub-instruction/sub-trajectory matching through attention and through representations.
insight: Only the abstract was available, so no ablation evidence can be cited. The abstract implies that explicit fine-grained alignment supervision, using the sub-instruction annotations in Landmark-RxR, gives extra learning signal that improves decision-making beyond the navigation loss alone.
method: Attention Alignment Constraint (AAC): an auxiliary supervision signal on the agent's attention so that it focuses on the sub-instruction matching the current sub-trajectory.
Representation Alignment Constraint (RAC): an auxiliary supervision signal on representations that aligns sub-trajectory and sub-instruction features.
AFAC: AAC and RAC are combined as auxiliary training losses alongside the navigation objective.

setting.simulator: not specified in the abstract (photo-realistic environments)
setting.privileged: Not stated; fine-grained sub-instruction alignment annotations from Landmark-RxR are probably used as training supervision.

results: The abstract claims state-of-the-art results on the Landmark-RxR benchmark in both seen and unseen environments, but gives no numbers or named baselines.
limitations: Only the abstract was available, so details on the backbone, metrics and ablations are missing.
The method likely depends on fine-grained sub-instruction alignment annotations such as those in Landmark-RxR.
